answer: Require each agent identity to continuously produce fresh proof-of-work bound to its own key: a compute puzzle that cannot be reused or shared across identities. An attacker must then pay real electricity and hardware per fake agent, every epoch, so a thousand sockpuppets cost a thousand times more than one. Honest agents that wander across tasks keep proofs cheap because one key does one stream of work, while the horizon of cheap forgery closes: like crossing a tundra, every extra mile of fake identity costs real energy, and the network can simply raise puzzle difficulty when sybils appear.
